database_summary: This is a sports/entertainment (pro-wrestling) event schema. Core entities are promotions, cards (events on a given date/location/promotion), matches (individual matches on a card), wrestlers, belts, match types, locations, and scraped HTML tables. Data includes event metadata (Cards, Events, Locations, Promotions) and many Matches (event-level child records). Matches are the largest fact table (~540k rows).

accepted.name: cards_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Cards.id AS id,
  Cards.table_id AS table_id,
  Cards.location_id AS location_id,
  Cards.promotion_id AS promotion_id,
  Cards.event_date AS event_date,
  Cards.event_id AS event_id,
  Cards.url AS url,
  Cards.info_html AS info_html,
  Cards.match_html AS match_html,
  Promotions.id AS Promotion_id,
  Promotions.name AS Promotion_name,
  Locations.id AS Location_id,
  Locations.name AS Location_name,
  Events.id AS Event_id,
  Events.name AS Event_name,
  Tables.id AS Table_id,
  Tables.html AS Table_html,
  Tables.url AS Table_url
FROM Cards
LEFT JOIN Promotions ON Cards.promotion_id = Promotions.id
LEFT JOIN Locations ON Cards.location_id = Locations.id
LEFT JOIN Events ON Cards.event_id = Events.id
LEFT JOIN Tables ON Cards.table_id = Tables.id
accepted.description: One row per Card enriched with linked Promotion, Location, Event, and Table metadata. Use this when you need card-level attributes (date, venue, promotion) alongside source HTML/url for joins to Matches or for event-level reporting. | Use for: List cards (shows) with promotion and location names; Filter cards by promotion/location/date range; Join matches to card metadata or original scraped HTML

accepted.name: matches_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Matches.id AS id,
  Matches.card_id AS card_id,
  Matches.winner_id AS winner_id,
  Matches.loser_id AS loser_id,
  Matches.win_type AS win_type,
  Matches.match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  Matches.duration AS duration,
  -- parse duration MM:SS to integer seconds; empty or unparsable -> NULL
  (CASE
    WHEN length(trim(Matches.duration)) = 0 THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(Matches.duration, ':') > 0 THEN (
      CASE
        WHEN cast(substr(Matches.duration, 1, instr(Matches.duration, ':')-1) AS integer) IS NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE (
          cast(substr(Matches.duration, 1, instr(Matches.duration, ':')-1) AS integer) * 60
          + cast(substr(Matches.duration, instr(Matches.duration, ':')+1) AS integer)
        )
      END
    )
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS duration_seconds,
  Matches.title_id AS title_id,
  Matches.title_change AS title_change,
  Matches.win_type AS win_type_dup
FROM Matches
accepted.description: Normalized Matches at one row per match. Preserves raw winner/loser identifiers and exposes parsed duration_seconds and title_change flag. Use this as the canonical matches fact for counting matches, filtering by duration, or joining to Wrestlers/Belts/Match_Types. | Use for: Count matches, filter by duration ranges, detect title changes; Join matches to Wrestlers/Belts/Match_Types and Cards; Aggregate match-level statistics per wrestler or card

accepted.name: matches_with_card
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.card_id AS card_id,
  c.event_date AS event_date,
  c.promotion_id AS promotion_id,
  c.location_id AS location_id,
  c.event_id AS event_id,
  m.winner_id AS winner_id,
  m.loser_id AS loser_id,
  m.win_type AS win_type,
  m.match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  m.duration AS duration,
  m.title_id AS title_id,
  m.title_change AS title_change
FROM Matches m
LEFT JOIN Cards c ON m.card_id = c.id
accepted.description: One row per Match with card-level context (event_date, promotion, location) by joining Matches to Cards and Promotions/Locations/Events. Use this for temporal or promotion-based match analysis. | Use for: Trends of matches by promotion or location over time; Find matches at a given venue or promotion; Aggregate matches per card or per date

accepted.name: wrestler_match_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.id AS id,
  w.name AS name,
  COALESCE(win_counts.total_wins, 0) + COALESCE(loss_counts.total_losses, 0) AS total_matches,
  COALESCE(win_counts.total_wins, 0) AS wins,
  COALESCE(loss_counts.total_losses, 0) AS losses,
  COALESCE(title_counts.title_change_count, 0) AS title_changes
FROM Wrestlers w
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT winner_id AS wrestler_id, COUNT(*) AS total_wins
  FROM Matches
  WHERE winner_id IS NOT NULL AND trim(winner_id) <> ''
  GROUP BY winner_id
) win_counts ON win_counts.wrestler_id = cast(w.id AS TEXT)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT loser_id AS wrestler_id, COUNT(*) AS total_losses
  FROM Matches
  WHERE loser_id IS NOT NULL AND trim(loser_id) <> ''
  GROUP BY loser_id
) loss_counts ON loss_counts.wrestler_id = cast(w.id AS TEXT)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT winner_id AS wrestler_id, COUNT(*) AS title_change_count
  FROM Matches
  WHERE title_change = 1 AND winner_id IS NOT NULL AND trim(winner_id) <> ''
  GROUP BY winner_id
) title_counts ON title_counts.wrestler_id = cast(w.id AS TEXT)
accepted.description: Aggregated counts of matches and title changes per Wrestler id (as winner or loser). Produces one row per Wrestler.id with total_matches, wins, losses, and title_changes. Useful for leaderboards and career summaries. | Use for: Top wrestlers by wins/losses/total matches; Career title change counts per wrestler; Create win-loss records for wrestlers

accepted.name: match_type_popularity
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  mt.id AS id,
  mt.name AS name,
  COALESCE(cnt.match_count, 0) AS match_count
FROM Match_Types mt
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT match_type_id, COUNT(*) AS match_count
  FROM Matches
  WHERE match_type_id IS NOT NULL AND trim(match_type_id) <> ''
  GROUP BY match_type_id
) cnt ON cnt.match_type_id = cast(mt.id AS TEXT)
accepted.description: Counts of matches per Match_Types.id with the type name. One row per match_type_id with match_count. Useful for understanding which match types are most common. | Use for: Rank match types by frequency; Filter match types with at least N matches (N applied downstream); Analyze distribution of match formats over time (join to Cards)

accepted.name: cards_ranked_by_date
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.promotion_id AS promotion_id,
  c.event_date AS event_date,
  c.location_id AS location_id,
  c.event_id AS event_id,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.promotion_id ORDER BY c.event_date DESC) AS promotion_card_rank
FROM Cards c
accepted.description: Cards with a row_number per promotion ordered by event_date (most recent first). Exposes promotion_card_rank so downstream queries can select top-K recent cards per promotion without embedding ordering logic. | Use for: Most recent N cards per promotion; Temporal sampling of cards per promotion; Combine with Matches to fetch matches from latest shows per promotion

accepted.name: matches_running_count_per_card
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.card_id AS card_id,
  m.winner_id AS winner_id,
  m.loser_id AS loser_id,
  m.duration AS duration,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.card_id ORDER BY m.id) AS match_position,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY m.card_id) AS matches_per_card
FROM Matches m
accepted.description: For each match on a card, expose a match_position (1..N) within its card ordered by Matches.id. Useful to pick opening/midcard/main events or compute running tallies per card. | Use for: Identify main events (highest match_position) or opening matches; Distribute match-level metrics relative to card position; Filter matches by being the last/first on a card
